newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares soar to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares soar to new highs.

text.p: Oil shares on the Nigerian bourse rose to new highs in speculative Friday trade, dealers said.
The gains pushed the all-share index up 29.15 points to 6775.61 from 6746.46, its biggest one-day rise this week.
Some dealers grumbled at the development, saying there was no information to warrant big gains but the bulls justified their action by the standard "market forces" argument.
African Petroleum and Total rose 80 kobo apiece to 41.00 naira and 54.00 naira, respectively. Mobil closed at 46.00 naira and National Oil at 43.20 naira, each adding 70 kobo.
Unipetrol was 40 kobo up at 52.00 naira while Texaco and Agip were 30 kobo stronger at 30.50 naira and 18.75 naira, respectively.
Traders said the oil sector would remain in the commanding position in the next few weeks as speculators jostle for a share of the big price gains.
Food and breweries firms also fared better.

Nigerian Breweries bounced to 15.60 naira with a 40 kobo gain while Guinness added 20 kobo to 6.30 naira. Nigerian Breweries' rally was consolidated on Thursday by an improved nine-month result, said dealers.
Strong demand for Nestle earned it a 70 kobo rise to 45.20 naira. Union Dicon Salt also chalked up 26 kobo to 41.88 naira as National Salt company added 10 kobo to 6.10 naira.
But Conglomerates and banks were worse off.
Guaranty Trust Bank shed 15 kobo at 12.80 naira. NAL Merchant Bank and Union Bank lost 10 kobo each at 4.90 naira and 5.80 naira, respectively.
UAC slid by 30 kobo to 8.40 naira, overtaking Lever Brothers as the biggest loser in the conglomerates sector. Lever Brothers fell by 20 kobo to 22.30 naira.
Leading food company Cadbury, however, closed 10 kobo lower on the surplus shares in the market. It ended at 24.70 naira.
Benue and Ashaka Cement lost some of their recent gains on Friday. Benue fell 25 kobo to 7.80 naira while Ashaka slid by 10 kobo to 18.45 naira on fears that sales were slowing.
Traders said if new results confirm falling profits, these companies' shares might take further knocks on the trading floor.
